阿索斯山上的各个族群共同体，有时拿“语言”来称呼。
《罗萨诺的圣尼洛斯传》（十世纪）把基督徒分为两类：一类是与圣徒“同种族”的人（
），另一类是“讲不同语言”的人（
普塞洛斯在写给一位离开首都的朋友的信中问道：“倘若我是一个意大利人或布立吞人，生活在许多讲着许多不同语言的外族人中间，难道我不会用他们所有人去换一个同
（genos）的人吗？”
另一方面，语言并非族群性的唯一标准。一个罗马人可以讲外语、甚至通双语而不失其为罗马人，
反之，外族人可以讲希腊语却并不因此被视为罗马人。例如，保加尔沙皇西美昂（卒于927年）能讲希腊语，因为他童年部分时间在帝国宫廷度过，也许他认为这使他有资格角逐罗马皇位。罗马人试图剥夺他的一切资格凭证，其中也包括他的语言能力。一位罗马演说家明确指出：“西美昂说起话来多半像个蛮族人，语病百出。”

en: Two incidents from military history show how language could be used to literally patrol the boundaries between ethnic groups. In a war with Persia in the late sixth century, the Romans gave their barbarian allies a password, the name of the Mother of God
so that they might know each other in battle and not “mistake their allies as enemies and kill them because of their difference in
In the twelfth century, when some Roman commanders attacked the Turks at night, they issued the password
(iron), which only the Romans could pronounce. The historian remarked that this allowed them to recognize the
(people of the same race) based on their
(speaking the same language), because the inability to say the word proved who was
(a foreign-speaker).
This was the Roman equivalent of the shibboleth story in the Old Testament: even minor differences in speech patterns could lead to the execution of an out-group member.
zh: 军事史上的两个事件表明，族群之间的边界如何真能借语言来守卫。六世纪晚期与波斯的一场战争中，罗马人给他们的蛮族盟友一个口令，即童贞圣母的名号（
），以便他们在战斗中彼此辨认，不至于“因
（genos）不同而误把盟友当敌人杀掉”。
十二世纪，当一些罗马指挥官夜袭突厥人时，他们定下了口令
（铁），这个词只有罗马人能正确发音。历史学家评论说，这使他们能根据
（homophonon，讲相同语言）辨认
（homophylon，同种族之人），因为说不出这个词就证明谁是
（alloglotton，讲外语之人）。
这是罗马版的《旧约》“示播列”故事：即便发音上的细微差别，也可能让外族人丧命。

en: But in the case of the Byzantine Romans there was a twist in the otherwise straightforward equation of language and nation. In antiquity, the main language of the Romans, the Roman language, or “Roman,” was Latin. Latin could also be called the language of the Latins, or some variation thereof. Even though many ancient Romans, especially elites, also spoke Greek, so much so that they referred to “our two languages,” Latin was regarded as “the language of the Romans,” an idea that continued into Byzantine times.

This meant that Byzantine authors, who wrote in Greek, referred to what had effectively become a foreign language to them, Latin, as the language of the Romans, even though they were now the Romans, in fact the only Romans in the world, except for those of Rome in Italy. They referred to “the language of the Romans” whenever someone in a narrative spoke Latin (which included both conversation and formulaic acclamations by the army or imperial subjects), as well as when the author had to use a technical term or the name of an office that was derived from Latin. These foreign terms jarred with the purist Hellenic diction to which many elite Byzantine authors aspired. All this has been laid out in a persuasive study by Carolina Cupane.
zh: 但对拜占庭罗马人而言，语言与民族的对应关系却多了一层曲折。在古代，罗马人的主要语言、罗马语言、或“罗马语”，是拉丁语。拉丁语也可称作“拉丁人的语言”，或用近似的说法来称呼。尽管许多古代罗马人、尤其是精英也讲希腊语，以至于他们提到“我们的两种语言”，拉丁语仍被视为“罗马人的语言”，这一观念延续到拜占庭时代。

这意味着以希腊语写作的拜占庭作者，把实际上已成为他们外语的拉丁语称为罗马人的语言，尽管他们如今才是罗马人，事实上是世上唯一的罗马人（意大利罗马城的罗马人除外）。每当叙事中有人讲拉丁语（包括对话以及军队或帝国臣民的程式化欢呼），以及当作者不得不使用一个源自拉丁语的术语或官职名称时，他们就提到“罗马人的语言”。这些外来词与许多精英拜占庭作者所追求的纯正希腊措辞相抵牾。卡罗琳娜·库帕内在一项有说服力的研究中已阐明这一切。

en: Two areas of Byzantine life were seen as especially “Roman” from a linguistic point of view because they contained a greater density of Latin terms: these were law and the army. Law was sometimes even called the study of the Roman matters or the Italian science. Byzantine legal dictionaries could be called “collections of Roman words.”
By contrast, the Byzantines called the language in which they spoke and wrote “Hellenic” or “Greek.” Some of them knew that it was the
dialect.

In its spoken forms, however, it was a heavily Latinized version of Greek. Thousands of Latin terms for everyday objects and activities had entered the Greek language between the second and the sixth centuries, and many of them survive still in spoken Greek.
To write formal Greek, Byzantine authors had to learn to filter those terms out so as not to sound too vernacular—or too Latin—just as they avoided the term
zh: 拜占庭生活有两个领域从语言角度看被视为特别“罗马”，因为它们含有更高密度的拉丁词：法律与军队。法律有时甚至被称为研究罗马事务的学问，或意大利之学。拜占庭法律词典可被称为“罗马词汇汇编”。
相比之下，拜占庭人把他们口头与书面使用的语言称为“希腊语”（Hellenic 或 Greek）。他们中有些人知道它属于希腊
（koine）。
然而在其口语形式中，它是一种高度拉丁化的希腊语。数千个指称日常物品与活动的拉丁词在二至六世纪之间进入希腊语，其中许多仍存于口语希腊语中。
为了撰写正式希腊语，拜占庭作者得学会避开那些词，以免显得过于口语化，或拉丁色彩太重——正如他们回避
一词。

en: While this usage was conventional, it sometimes put the Byzantines in an awkward situation. Why would “the language of the Romans” be different from the language currently spoken by the Romans? This was, after all, what western critics (such as popes and German emperors) brought forward in order to deny that the Byzantines were really Romans. In a famous letter of 865, Pope Nicolaus I scolded the emperor Michael III for calling himself the emperor of the Romans when he did not speak the language of the Romans (i.e., Latin); it seems that Michael had even denigrated the Latin language in his now lost letter.
Some modern Greek scholars make the same error: the Byzantines were really Greeks, they assert, because they spoke Greek.
zh: 虽然这种用法是惯例，它有时却使拜占庭人陷入尴尬境地。为什么“罗马人的语言”会不同于罗马人当下所讲的语言？这毕竟正是西方批评者（如教皇与德意志皇帝）用来否认拜占庭人是真正罗马人的论据。在865年一封著名的信中，教皇尼古拉一世斥责皇帝米海尔三世自称罗马人的皇帝，却不会讲罗马人的语言（即拉丁语）；似乎米海尔甚至在他那封现已佚失的信中贬低了拉丁语。
一些现代希腊学者犯同样的错误：他们断言拜占庭人其实是希腊人，因为他们讲希腊语。

en: The Byzantines had ways of addressing this mismatch of language and ethnicity, but it should be noted that at no point did this discrepancy cause them to doubt whether they were Romans. Until the end of the empire and beyond, they were unpersuaded by western polemics on this point. Moreover, our understanding of ethnicity should give to the Byzantines themselves the right to decide which of their cultural attributes constituted their ethnicity and how. Here the evidence is clear: they did not see their ethnicity as defined by their language, but the reverse.
zh: 拜占庭人有办法应对语言与族群性的这种错位，但应当指出，这种不一致在任何时候都未使他们怀疑自己是否是罗马人。直到帝国终结乃至其后，他们在这一点上都不为西方的论战所动。此外，我们对族群性的理解应当赋予拜占庭人自己以权利，去决定他们的哪些文化属性构成其族群性、以及如何构成。这里证据是清楚的：在他们看来，是自己的族群身份界定了语言的归属。

en: One device was to qualify Latin as “the

language” of the Romans, implying that it was no longer the language that they used, but was the language of their ancestors. This reinforced the ethnic connection between the Byzantines and the ancient Romans. We can even observe the invention of this linguistic ancestry, which occurred at the same time as the rise and establishment of the notion of Romanía. Consider, for example, Themistios, who was a leading member of the Senate of Constantinople and a Hellenist (pagan) philosopher in the fourth century. For all that he was deeply embroiled in Roman things, he had not yet “converted” to a Roman ethnicity, just as he had not converted to Christianity. He begins one of his speeches addressed to the emperors with a declaration that he has not found it necessary to master the “ruling language” because his “ancestral Greek language was sufficient.”

But two centuries later, the referent of linguistic ancestry had changed from Greek to Latin, even among intellectuals from the Greek east whose native language was Greek. The scholar Ioannes Lydos was from western Asia Minor and was awarded a chair of Latin in Constantinople under Justinian. Even though he wrote in Greek, he lamented that the administration of the empire was being conducted increasingly in Greek and not in “the ancestral language of the Romans,” Latin.
The seventh-century historian Theophylaktos, a native of Egypt writing in Constantinople, frequently refers to Latin as the ancestral language.
zh: 一种手法是称拉丁语为罗马人的“

”，暗示它不再是他们使用的语言，而是他们祖先的语言。这强化了拜占庭人与古罗马人之间的族群联系。我们甚至可以观察到这一关于祖先语言的观念是如何形成的，它与罗曼尼亚观念的兴起和确立同时发生。例如塞米斯提乌斯，他是四世纪君士坦丁堡元老院的主要成员，也是一位希腊主义（异教）哲学家。尽管他深深卷入罗马事务，他却尚未“皈入”罗马族群，正如他并未皈依基督教。他在一篇致皇帝的演说开头宣称，他认为没有必要掌握“统治的语言”，因为他的“祖传希腊语已经足够”。
但两个世纪后，就连来自讲希腊语的东部地区、母语是希腊语的知识分子，也由奉希腊语为祖传语言转为奉拉丁语为祖传语言。学者约安尼斯·吕多斯来自小亚细亚西部，在查士丁尼治下被授予君士坦丁堡的拉丁语教席。尽管他以希腊语写作，他却哀叹帝国的行政日益以希腊语而非“罗马人的祖传语言”拉丁语进行。
七世纪历史学家塞奥菲拉克托斯是埃及人，在君士坦丁堡写作，频繁地把拉丁语称为祖传语言。

en: This usage implied that at some point the Romans had stopped using their ancestral language and began to use Greek instead. We can observe that switch in real time in some of the laws of the emperor Justinian, who contributed to that switch. Justinian commented on the reasons behind his decision to stop issuing his
in the “ancestral language” of the Romans and to use Greek instead: it was now the language of the majority of subjects.

Looking back at this switch four centuries later, Konstantinos VII wrote that emperors after Herakleios (610–641) “Hellenized [i.e., used Greek] to an even greater degree and cast off their ancestral Roman language.”
zh: 这种用法暗示，罗马人在某个时刻停止使用其祖传语言，转而开始使用希腊语。我们可以在皇帝查士丁尼的一些法律中看到这场变化发生时的情形，查士丁尼本人也参与了这一转变。查士丁尼解释了他为何不再用罗马人的“祖传语言”颁布《新律》（
），改用希腊语，因为当时多数臣民说的是希腊语。
四个世纪后回顾这一转变，君士坦丁七世写道，希拉克略（610–641年在位）之后的皇帝们“更大程度地希腊化［即使用希腊语］，并抛弃了他们的祖传罗马语言”。

en: It is impossible to know how many average Romans in Byzantium knew that the language of their ancestors had been Latin. But the mentality of those who did is interesting. To maintain the fiction of their Roman ethnic origin, and to reinforce the obvious truth of imperial continuity, they were willing to posit a rupture in the linguistic continuity of their own ethnic history. This proves how deeply they identified as Romans: no self-identifying ethnic “Greek” would ever refer to Latin as his ancestral language. This is not without parallel in other times or parts of the world, mutatis mutandis. The ancestral language of Greek-speaking Jews in antiquity was Hebrew. The ancestral language of Ireland is Gaelic. Latin in Byzantium can be seen as such a “talismanic” ancestral language, analogous to Hebrew among postbiblical Jews: “a national language that is not spoken by most of the nation.”

This talisman was invoked when authors had to explain the name of a Latin office, a vernacular Latin term that linked Romanía to its ancient roots, or the ritualized acclamations that preserved many Latinate fossils within spoken Greek.
zh: 无法知道拜占庭有多少普通罗马人知道其祖先的语言曾是拉丁语。但那些知道者的心态很有趣。为了维持罗马族群出身这一虚构，并强调帝国延续这一显而易见的事实，他们愿意承认自身族群的语言传承曾经中断。这证明他们作为罗马人的认同有多深：没有一个自我认同为族群“希腊人”的人会把拉丁语称为自己的祖传语言。其他时代和地区也有可以比照的例子，具体情形各有不同。古代讲希腊语的犹太人的祖传语言是希伯来语。爱尔兰的祖传语言是盖尔语。拜占庭的拉丁语可被视为这样一种“护符般的”祖传语言，类似于后圣经时代犹太人中的希伯来语：“一种民族语言，但这个民族的大多数人并不说它。”
当作者不得不解释一个拉丁官职的名称、一个把罗曼尼亚与其古老根源相连的通俗拉丁词、或解释那些在希腊口语中保留了众多拉丁语遗存的仪式性欢呼语时，就会搬出这道护符。

en: However, the fine distinction between the ancestral and current language of the Romans likely preoccupied few Byzantines. The majority of the population was, in the middle Byzantine period, coming to a more straightforward view of the relationship between their Romanness and their language. Not caring for the historical claims of Latin or the niceties of linguistic accuracy, they began on a popular level to call their (Greek) language “Roman,” because they were Romans and that was their language. It is likely that they were doing so for a long time before our sources catch up to the fact. This corresponds to how popular speech pioneered the name Romanía for the national state of the Romans, before more official types of discourse caught up.
zh: 然而，罗马人的祖传语言和现用语言之间的微妙区别，大概很少有拜占庭人会在意。拜占庭中期，多数人开始更直接地理解罗马身份与语言的关系。一般民众不去计较拉丁语在历史上的地位，也不讲究语言分类有多精确，开始把自己的语言（希腊语）叫作“罗马语”，因为他们是罗马人，说的就是这种语言。史料记下这种叫法以前，他们很可能早就这样称呼了。罗曼尼亚这个国名也是如此，先由民间用来指罗马人的民族国家，后来才见于较正式的话语。

en: In spoken Greek, the change to naming the language “Romaic” was complete and comprehensive by 1250. We have two foreign sources for this development, which come from different parts of the former empire and are independent of each other. The
composed by Greek-speaking Franks in the Peloponnese, calls the (Greek) speech of the locals Romaic (ῥωμαίικα).

On the other side of the Aegean, in Muslim-ruled Asia Minor, Sultan Veled (Walad, late thirteenth century), the son of the great Persian poet Jalal al-Din Rumi, wrote a poem in which he addresses a beautiful woman in Greek, so she can understand him; he precisely transcribes his words of seduction in which he calls the language Romaic (ῥωμαϊκά).
Thus, independent Frankish and Persian witnesses, living at opposite ends of the former empire, attest that the language of the Byzantines was being called
or
among provincials who had nothing to do with the literary conventions of the imperial court. The attestation of this term in non-Roman sources signals that it may have been

to appear in texts written in high-register Greek, even if it had been in use for many centuries. Here again our elite sources downplay the extent of popular Romanness. In this case they may have done so not only to avoid the newfangled term
which came from vulgar Greek, but also because they positively wanted to retain the talismanic valence of claiming a connection to Latin as the language of the Roman ancestors.
zh: 到1250年，人们在口语中已普遍将自己讲的希腊语称为“罗马语”（Romaic）。关于这一发展我们有两份外族史料，它们来自原帝国疆域内的不同地区且彼此独立。《摩里亚编年史》由伯罗奔尼撒讲希腊语的法兰克人撰写，把当地人的（希腊）语言称为罗马语（ῥωμαίικα）。
在爱琴海另一侧、穆斯林统治的小亚细亚，苏丹维莱德（瓦拉德，十三世纪晚期）——伟大的波斯诗人贾拉勒丁·鲁米之子——写了一首诗，用希腊语向一位美女倾诉，以便她能听懂；他精确转写了自己的求爱之辞，其中把该语言称为罗马语（ῥωμαϊκά）。
因此，法兰克和波斯的两份独立见证分别来自旧帝国的两端，表明那些与宫廷写作惯例毫无关系的行省居民管拜占庭人的语言叫
或
。这个称呼见于非罗马史料，这表明，它可能
，以至于无法出现在以高雅希腊语体写成的文本中，即便它已被使用了许多个世纪。精英文献在这里再次掩盖了罗马认同在民间的普及程度。在这种情况下，他们这样做可能不仅是为了回避来自通俗希腊语的新奇术语
（Romaic），也因为他们有意继续宣称自己与罗马祖先的语言拉丁语有联系，让这种联系继续发挥护符般的作用。

en: There is no reason to think that the

or Sultan Veled were reflecting a new convention in calling Greek “Romaic.” This is what they heard and learned from provincial Greek-speakers in the post-Byzantine Peloponnese and Asia Minor. Now, those two regions had parted ways in 1204, so the name used for their language by provincial Romans was probably already in place before then, and possibly before the 1070s, when the Seljuks first overran central Asia Minor.
zh: 没有理由认为《摩里亚编年史》或苏丹维莱德反映的是一种把希腊语称为“罗马语”的新惯例。这是他们在后拜占庭时代的伯罗奔尼撒与小亚细亚从行省讲希腊语者那里听到并学来的。而这两个地区在1204年分道扬镳，因此行省罗马人用来称呼其语言的名称很可能在那之前就已确立，甚至可能在1070年代之前——那时塞尔柱人首次席卷小亚细亚中部。

en: This development was bound to happen. A Roman ethnic group was eventually going to start calling its language “the language of the Romans.” Even court sources sometimes did this. For example, when the biography of the emperor Basileios I (written in the tenth century) says that barbarian spies were sent out using Roman dress and language, the latter was obviously Greek.

And while it was common for Byzantine authors to describe terms of Latin origin that were used in contemporary spoken Greek as “Roman” words, they could also explain Greek technical terms as being words in the language of the “Romans,” that is, the (Byzantine) Romans of their own day.
On a vernacular level, the poem
says that the hero’s father, a Saracen by origin, knew “the language of the Romans,” also meaning Greek.
And when the Georgian general Gregorios Pakourianos endowed a monastery in Bulgaria in 1083 after years of imperial service, he used
for the Greek language and script of the charter.

This was a usage that he likely picked up during his years of service, not from an education in formal Greek. This reinforces the conclusion that “Roman” was the name given to their language by average Romans in the mid-eleventh century, and possibly earlier too. This evidence refutes the notion that spoken Greek came to be called Romaic only in the Ottoman period.
zh: 这一发展注定会发生。罗马族群迟早会开始把自己的语言称为“罗马人的语言”。甚至宫廷史料有时也这样做。例如，皇帝瓦西里一世的传记（写于十世纪）说，蛮族间谍身着罗马服饰、使用罗马语言被派出，后者显然是希腊语。
虽然拜占庭作者常把用于当时口语希腊语的拉丁源词描述为“罗马”词，他们也能把希腊语术语解释为“罗马人”语言中的词，即他们自己那个时代的（拜占庭）罗马人。
在通俗层面，诗作《迪格尼斯》说英雄的父亲——原是萨拉森人——懂“罗马人的语言”，同样指希腊语。
而当格鲁吉亚将军格里戈里奥斯·帕库里亚诺斯在多年帝国服役后于1083年在保加利亚捐建一座修道院时，他用
指称那份文书所用的希腊语和字母。
这种用法很可能是他在服役期间学来的，来源并非正规的希腊语教育。这强化了如下结论：“罗马”是十一世纪中叶普通罗马人给予其语言的名称，可能更早亦然。这一证据驳斥了口语希腊语直到奥斯曼时期才被称为罗马语的观念。

en: Romaic as “Greek” appears more frequently in the later Byzantine period. For example, the translation of the romance
is (strangely to our ears) called a “translation from Latin into Roman” (μεταγλώττισμα ἀπὸ λατινικὸν εἰς Ρωμαϊκόν).

Roman was here juxtaposed to Latin. In addition to being a vernacular term for Greek, Romaic may also have been a term for vernacular Greek as opposed to Attic or elite Greek. Elizabeth Fisher has brought attention to a translation of an

made from Arabic into Greek by a certain Alexios around 1245. A second Greek translator of the text commented that Alexios had transposed the text into “Hellenic, which is to say into Romaic.” The second translator accordingly tried to elevate the style into a higher register of Greek.

Romaic may here stand for a less elevated form of Greek, closer to what was being spoken. This distinction persisted, on and off in various contexts, until recently. A priest in Serres in the seventeenth century drew a firm contrast between Romaic and Hellenic writing, the latter accessible only to teachers and scholars. In the early years of the nineteenth century, it was still seen as bizarre to call the spoken language “modern Greek” rather than “Romaic, which is how the entire nation calls it.” And a Russian newspaper in 1821 distinguished between ancient Greek and modern Greek, calling the latter “Romaic.”
Philologists were already comparing Romaic Greek to classical Greek on the one hand and to Latin on the other.
zh: 拜占庭晚期，以“罗马语”指希腊语的用例更常见了。例如，传奇《推罗王阿波罗尼乌斯》的译本（在我们听来很奇怪）被称为“从拉丁语译为罗马语”（μεταγλώττισμα ἀπὸ λατινικὸν εἰς Ρωμαϊκόν）。
这里罗马语与拉丁语并置。“罗马语”除了是希腊语的俗称，也可能专指希腊俗语，有别于阿提卡语或精英所用的希腊语。伊丽莎白·费舍尔让人注意到一部《但以理启示录》，由某个阿莱克修斯约在1245年从阿拉伯语译为希腊语。该文本的第二位希腊语译者评论说，阿莱克修斯把文本转成了“希腊语，也就是说罗马语”。第二位译者于是试图把文体提升到更高的希腊语体。
罗马语在这里可能代表一种不那么高雅的希腊语形式，更接近口头所讲。这一区别在各种语境中时断时续地存续，直到晚近。十七世纪塞雷斯的一位教士在罗马语与希腊语写作之间划出明确对照，后者只有教师与学者才能掌握。十九世纪初年，把口语称为“现代希腊语”而非“罗马语——整个民族都这样称呼它”仍被视为怪异。而1821年一家俄国报纸区分古希腊语与现代希腊语，把后者称为“罗马语”。
语文学家已经开始把这种叫作罗马语的希腊语分别与古典希腊语和拉丁语加以比较。

en: This Roman “nation” continued to exist during the centuries of Ottoman domination and, contrary to widespread belief, was never fully subsumed within a pan-Orthodox community (the

of Rum). The Romans continued to be set off by roughly the same ethnic markers as they had in the past, if no longer by a separate state of their own. Consider, for example, how one hostile text describes the patriarch of Constantinople, Raphael I (1475–1476), who was of Serbian origin: “The people hated him, because of his habitual drunkenness and also because of his speech, as he did not speak
only Serbian; as we said, he was from Serbia and spoke Serbian, whereas he spoke
only imperfectly.”
These distinctions were observed by non-Romans too. The seventeenth-century Ottoman travel writer Evliya Çelebi also classified as an ethnic Roman (
or
) whoever spoke what to his ears sounded like the
language.
The eighteenth-century travel writer Richard Chandler admits in one place that the nation he has been calling Greek really calls itself, and its language, “Roman.”
zh: 这个罗马“民族”在奥斯曼统治的数世纪中继续存在，而且与普遍看法相反，从未被完全纳入泛正教共同体（鲁姆
）。罗马人虽已没有自己的独立国家，仍凭借与过去大体相同的族群标志同其他人区分开来。例如，看看一份敌对文本如何描述君士坦丁堡牧首拉斐尔一世（1475–1476年在位），他出身塞尔维亚：“民众憎恨他，因为他惯常酗酒，也因为他的言语，因为他不讲
（Romaíika），只讲塞尔维亚语；如我们所说，他来自塞尔维亚、讲塞尔维亚语，而他讲
只讲得不地道。”
这些区别也被非罗马人观察到。十七世纪奥斯曼旅行作家埃夫利亚·切莱比也依此辨认族群，只要一个人说的话听上去像
（Rumca），他就把这个人归为罗马人（
或
十八世纪旅行作家理查德·钱德勒在一处承认，他一直称为希腊的那个民族其实把自己及其语言称为“罗马”。

en: According to the evidence presented above, the Greek language began to be popularly called Romaic no later than the eleventh century, and possibly earlier. We may be able to confirm this development and move it earlier in time with the help of Hebrew and Arabic evidence, though this will require further research by specialists. Byzantine Hebrew texts of the middle and later periods typically call Greek “the Roman tongue
” as the Jews of the empire are also conventionally called “the communities of Romanía.”

It is likely that the Jews were using the same name to refer to the language as was being used by their Christian neighbors, so it would be useful to date the earliest emergence of this usage among them. Arab authors too, writing outside of Romanía, often refer to the language spoken by the Rum as
(“in the tongue of the Romans”), in some cases distinguishing it from the Greek used by the ancient authors, which for them was

Intellectuals in the Arab Muslim world debated what the relationship was between the two languages, and al-Ya’qubi (d. 897) even claimed that the “Roman language” had replaced Greek after the Roman conquest.
It would be interesting to know if
was merely an Arabic rendition of what Romans whom they met—including soldiers, merchants, and captives—were calling their own speech (“the language of the Romans”).
zh: 根据上面呈现的证据，希腊语至迟在十一世纪就开始被民众称为罗马语，可能更早。借助希伯来语与阿拉伯语证据，我们或许能够证实这一发展并把它在时间上推前，尽管这需要专家的进一步研究。拜占庭中后期的希伯来语文本通常把希腊语称为“罗马人的语言”（
），正如帝国的犹太人也被惯常称为“罗曼尼亚的各犹太社群”。
很可能犹太人用来指称该语言的名称与其基督教邻人所用的相同，因此确定这一用法在他们中间最早出现的时间会很有用。在罗曼尼亚之外写作的阿拉伯作者也常把鲁姆人所讲的语言称为
（“用罗马人的语言”），有些情况下把它与古代作者所用的希腊语区分开来，后者对他们而言是
（希腊语）。阿拉伯穆斯林世界的知识分子争论这两种语言之间的关系，雅库比（卒于897年）甚至声称“罗马语言”在罗马征服后取代了希腊语。
值得追问的是，他们碰到的罗马人，包括士兵、商人和俘虏，是否就把自己的话称为“罗马人的语言”，而阿拉伯语的
只不过把这种自称照译了出来。

en: Be that as it may, the evidence presented above shows that the Romans’ ethnic self-understanding eventually overcame the terminological distinctions between Greek and Roman that they had inherited from antiquity, and created instead a separate, and quite fascinating, distinction between Roman and Latin. Their ethnicity and ethnonym overcame the conventional linguistic classification of their language. One of the main arguments used by western medieval writers and their modern followers to prove that the Byzantines were “really” Greeks is the fact that after about 600 they spoke Greek. This argument is also welcome to the modern Greek national interpretation of history, because more than anything it seems to authorize the rebaptism of the Romaioi as Greeks. As Greg Fisher has written, “the legacy of modern nationalism and modern ideas about linguistic identity can colour our understanding of how other, older, or different, cultures perceived themselves.”
Yet for most of their history the Byzantines did not think that their language made them Greek; to the contrary, their ethnicity as Romans made their language “Roman,” or Romaic.
zh: 无论如何，上面呈现的证据表明，罗马人的族群自我理解最终压过了古代遗留下来的“希腊”与“罗马”在术语上的区别，取而代之的是一道颇为引人注目的界线，分开了“罗马”与“拉丁”。他们的族群身份及族名改变了人们对他们所说语言的传统分类。西方中世纪作者及其现代追随者用来证明拜占庭人“其实”是希腊人的主要论据之一，是约600年之后他们讲希腊语这一事实。这一论据也受现代希腊民族主义历史解释的欢迎，因为它似乎比任何其他理由都更能让人把罗马人重新“洗礼”为希腊人。正如格雷格·费舍尔所写：“现代民族主义的遗产以及关于语言认同的现代观念，可能影响我们对其他文化自我认知的理解，无论那些文化更为古老，还是与我们的文化有所不同。”
然而在其历史的大部分时间里，拜占庭人并不认为语言使他们成为希腊人；恰恰相反，他们作为罗马人的族群性使他们的语言成为“罗马的”，即罗马语。

en: The Byzantines’ self-understanding in this matter did not deviate from ancient Roman precedents. In ancient Rome, Latin was at times invested with the aura of traditionalism but—and the following point cannot be repeated too much—there was never any requirement that one know Latin to be a Roman. Greek had always been a part of Roman culture and the Romans often referred to their “two languages,” Greek and Latin.
Interestingly, even Byzantines of the middle period could refer to their “two languages, Greek and Roman,” in some contexts, for example law.

The terms Roman and Latin were thus asymmetrical, and they remain so today. A study of ancient Roman literature might include Greek texts. A recent survey of Roman historiography, for example, begins with a senator writing in Greek (Fabius Pictor) and ends with both Greek and Latin historians of the later empire.

What was new about the Byzantines was not that they were Romans who spoke Greek but that they were Romans who had lost touch with the Latin tradition. That was an interesting development, though it emerged over the course of centuries.
zh: 拜占庭人在这件事上的自我理解并未偏离古罗马的先例。在古罗马，拉丁语有时带有尊崇古老传统的意味，但——以下这一点再怎么重复也不为过——成为罗马人从来就无须懂拉丁语。希腊语始终是罗马文化的一部分，罗马人常提到他们的“两种语言”，希腊语与拉丁语。
有趣的是，甚至中期拜占庭人在某些语境（例如法律）中也能提到他们的“两种语言，希腊语与罗马语”。
因此罗马与拉丁这两个术语是不对称的，今天依然如此。一项古罗马文学研究可能包含希腊语文本。例如，一部晚近的罗马史学概览以一位用希腊语写作的元老（法比乌斯·皮克托尔）开篇，以晚期帝国的希腊语与拉丁语历史学家作结。
拜占庭人的新之处不在于他们是讲希腊语的罗马人，而在于他们是与拉丁传统失去联系的罗马人。这个变化值得关注，不过它是在几个世纪里逐渐发生的。

en: Instead of arguing that the Byzantines were not really Romans because they did not speak Latin, we should be saying instead that the Byzantines had
Roman languages, one the language of their ancestors (Latin) and another their language in the present (Romaic).
zh: 我们不应论证拜占庭人因为不讲拉丁语就不是真正的罗马人，而应当说拜占庭人拥有
罗马语言，一种是其祖先的语言（拉丁语），另一种是其当下的语言（罗马语）。

en: Religion and Ethnicity
zh: 宗教与族群性

en: It was well understood in Byzantium—I believe by the entirety of the population—that the two labels Roman and (Orthodox) Christian did not signify the same thing, even though they overlapped when one was looking only at the Romans. Considerable efforts were made to fuse them together, for example in the title of the emperor, which became “faithful-in-Christ emperor of the Romans.” So too, provincial hagiographic texts could refer to the golden age before Islam “when the empire of the Romans was governed well by both orthodox doctrines and an excellent political system.”

Between the sixth and the ninth centuries, when the empire was surrounded mostly by barbarians who were also infidels, emperors could address their subjects as Christians rather than Romans in some contexts, because the two names pointed to the same population.
zh: 在拜占庭，人们——我认为是全体人口——都清楚明白，罗马与（正教）基督徒这两个标签并不指同一事物，尽管当只看罗马人时它们重叠。人们作了相当努力把它们融合在一起，例如皇帝的头衔变成了“在基督内忠信的罗马人皇帝”。同样，行省圣徒传文本可以提到伊斯兰之前的黄金时代，“那时罗马人的帝国治理有方，既有正统的教义，又有优良的政制”。
在六至九世纪之间，当帝国大多被既是蛮族又是异教徒的人包围时，皇帝在某些语境中可以称其臣民为基督徒而非罗马人，因为这两个名称指向同一人口。

en: Yet it was known that those two names were not equivalent and did not always overlap. For example, the Romans had formerly been quite hostile to the Christians. The average Byzantine would have been regularly reminded of this by the stories of the martyrs that were told in church, as they heard about cruel Roman officials gruesomely torturing Christian saints. Indeed, some early Christian literature is hostile to Rome, and in it “the name Roman and the name Christian are completely opposed.”

Conversely, there were many Christians in the present who were not Romans: the Franks were at first regarded as fellow Catholics (though not Romans) and then, when their Church began to deviate from received tradition, there were also the Bulgarians, Serbs, Georgians, and others. These were Orthodox but not Roman. Byzantine writers were quite capable of expressing the difference between their ethnic and religious identities. This did not require complicated theoretical distinctions on their part but was a matter of course. Already from the reign of Constantine, Christians were being divided into “Romans and
” (those of another race, e.g., Persians).
zh: 然而人们知道这两个名称并不等同，也并不总是重叠。例如，罗马人从前对基督徒相当敌视。普通拜占庭人会因教堂中讲述的殉道者故事而经常想起这一点，他们听到残酷的罗马官员惨无人道地折磨基督教圣徒。的确，一些早期基督教文献敌视罗马，其中“罗马之名与基督徒之名完全对立”。
反过来，在拜占庭人的时代，许多基督徒并非罗马人。法兰克人尽管并非罗马人，起初仍被视为同属公教。后来，当法兰克教会开始偏离沿袭下来的传统时，又有了保加尔人、塞尔维亚人、格鲁吉亚人等同道。这些人信奉正教，却都并非罗马人。拜占庭作者完全能够表达其族群认同与宗教认同之间的区别。这不需要他们作出复杂的理论区分，而是理所当然之事。早在君士坦丁统治时期，基督徒就被分为“罗马人与
（allophyloi）”（另一种族之人，如波斯人）。

en: Over time, Byzantine Romanness and Orthodoxy were closely intertwined and mutually encompassed each other: being Orthodox was part of the “customs and laws” that defined a Roman, while at the same time the Romans regarded themselves as the most important Christians in the world. Moreover, between the later sixth and mid-ninth centuries, the empire was surrounded on almost all sides by non-Christian peoples, so that “Roman” and “Christian” temporarily had the same boundaries. Roman patriotism could take the form of Christian zeal and vice versa. At such times, there was no compelling reason to distinguish the two conceptually. Roman and Christian could be used interchangeably not because they meant the same thing but because they referred to complementary identities of the same group of people.
That changed after the ninth century, especially with the conversion of Bulgaria.
zh: 随着时间推移，拜占庭的罗马性与正教信仰紧密交织、彼此涵盖：信奉正教是界定罗马人的“习俗与法律”的一部分，同时罗马人自视为世上最重要的基督徒。此外，在六世纪晚期至九世纪中叶之间，帝国几乎四面都被非基督教民族包围，因此“罗马”与“基督徒”所指的人群暂时重合。罗马爱国主义可以表现为基督教热忱，反之亦然。在这种时候，没有令人信服的理由在概念上区分二者。罗马与基督徒可以互换使用，不是因为它们指同一事物，而是因为它们指称同一群人的互补认同。
九世纪之后，这种情况发生了变化，尤其是在保加尔人皈依基督教以后。

en: All this is fairly straightforward and would not require much comment or excite any controversy were it not for the difficult circumstances in which the denialist tradition found itself when it morphed into a scholarly discipline of study in the late nineteenth and especially the twentieth century. Until the early nineteenth century, the west had been happy to relabel ethnic Romans as ethnic Greeks and leave the matter there, viewing them as Orthodox Christians as well. As we saw, the developments of that century made those labels problematic. The “Byzantines” were then uncoupled from any strong sense of Greek ethnicity and historians began to assert that they had no ethnicity. This left unresolved the problem of the pervasive ethnonym “Roman.” Some scholars decided to sweep this under the Christian rug, a move that is made in one of two contradictory ways, both false and arbitrary, that nevertheless have the same result. According to one fiction, “the Byzantines”
Romans anymore
Christians, whereas according to the other when the Byzantines said they were Romans they
only that they were Christians.

I hope it is clear by now that these unnecessary acrobatics obfuscate what is in fact an unproblematic situation: the Byzantines were Romans who were also Christians. This picture emerges clearly from the evidence and no reason has been offered why we should not take it at face value. Instead, there is only an entrenched and ideological obsession to deny that the Byzantines were Romans, by any pretext necessary. This impression has been given prima facie plausibility by the massive attention that was paid during the twentieth century to the Orthodox aspects of Byzantine civilization compared to the minimal attention (or negative attention) paid to its Roman aspects.
zh: 这一切都相当直截了当，本不需要多少评论或引发任何争议，若非否认论传统在十九世纪晚期、尤其是二十世纪演变为一门学科时陷入困境的话。直到十九世纪初，西方一直乐于把族群罗马人重新贴上族群希腊人的标签就此了事，同时也把他们视为正教徒。如我们所见，那个世纪的种种发展使那些标签成了问题。“拜占庭人”于是不再被视为有鲜明的希腊族群认同，历史学家开始断言他们没有族群性。这留下了无处不在的族名“罗马”这一问题未解决。一些学者搬出基督教来掩盖这个问题，办法有两种，彼此矛盾，也都武断而不实，结果却殊途同归。根据一种虚构，“拜占庭人”
罗马人
基督徒；而根据另一种，当拜占庭人说自己是罗马人时，他们
的只是自己是基督徒。
我希望到现在已经清楚，这些多此一举的论法把事情弄复杂了，情况本来很简单：拜占庭人是罗马人，同时也是基督徒。证据明明白白地指向这一点，至今也无人给出理由，说明为何不能据此理解。相反，只有一种根深蒂固的意识形态执念，要找遍借口否认拜占庭人是罗马人。二十世纪对拜占庭文明的正教面向关注甚多，对罗马面向则少有关注，也有论者给予负面评价，才使这种印象乍看之下似乎可信。

en: That the terms are not strictly interchangeable emerges when we try to replace one with the other in all contexts: saying that someone was a Christian by birth might make some amount of sense, but saying that he spoke the language of the Christians or dressed like a Christian does not. Let us look at some texts that reveal that Roman and Christian were not interchangeable. In the ninth century, Petros of Sicily wrote a treatise on the beliefs of a heretical group, the Paulicians, who had established a military stronghold at Tephrike in eastern Asia Minor, which he seems to have visited. He reports that they called themselves Christians and called “us” Romans in a religious sense. The Paulicians, in other words, were trying to depict Byzantine Orthodoxy as the “Roman religion,” not the true Christian faith; they had repurposed an ethnic label as a religious one. Petros, a priest, was baffled and outraged at this switch. He said that they were misusing “our ethnic name” in a religious sense in place of the main one that we use for our faith (“Christians”).
This encounter forced a Byzantine to confront his ethnic name being used as a religious label, and he thought it was completely wrongheaded.
zh: 这两个术语并非严格可互换，当我们试图在所有语境中以一个替换另一个时便显现出来：说某人天生是基督徒或许还有点道理，但说他讲基督徒的语言或穿得像基督徒则没有。让我们看一些揭示罗马与基督徒不可互换的文本。九世纪，西西里的彼得罗斯写了一篇论著，讨论一个异端群体保罗派的信仰，他们在小亚细亚东部的泰弗里凯建立了一个军事据点，他似乎到访过那里。他报告说，他们自称基督徒，并在宗教意义上称“我们”为罗马人。换言之，保罗派试图把拜占庭正教描绘为“罗马宗教”，而非真正的基督信仰；他们把一个族群标签挪用作宗教标签。彼得罗斯是一名教士，对这种转换既困惑又愤怒。他说他们在宗教意义上误用“我们的族名”，取代我们表明信仰时通常使用的称呼（“基督徒”）。
这种用法使一名拜占庭人不得不面对有人拿自己的族名来指宗教。他认为这大错特错。

en: The Bulgarians, Serbs, and Rus’ also converted to Byzantine Orthodoxy, but the Byzantines never regarded them as Romans. There is abundant evidence for this, and it is consistent.
I will give an example from the most remote province of the empire and another example from Constantinople. First, the

children: Life of Saint Neilos of Rossano

en: (tenth century) reports that when this southern Italian saint traveled to Rome he found a monastery twelve miles from the city “where a few brothers who were of the same race as he lived”

that is, fellow Greek-speakers. And the local clergy in Latin-occupied Constantinople told a Catholic cardinal in 1206 that they could, if they wanted, leave the City for one of the Byzantine successor states in exile or for “the lands of the barbarians who share our faith,” such as the Bulgarians or the Rus’.
A clear explanation was offered in the fifteenth century by Ioannes Kanaboutzes, who explained that
zh: 保加尔人、塞尔维亚人与罗斯人也皈依了拜占庭正教，但拜占庭人从未把他们视为罗马人。这方面证据丰富且一致。
我将举一个来自帝国最偏远行省的例子，以及另一个来自君士坦丁堡的例子。首先，《罗萨诺的圣尼洛斯传》（十世纪）报告说，当这位南意大利圣徒前往罗马时，他在距城十二英里处发现一座修道院，“那里住着几位与他同种族的弟兄”（
），即同为讲希腊语者。而在拉丁人占领的君士坦丁堡，当地教士1206年告诉一位公教枢机，他们若愿意，可以离开都城，前往某个拜占庭流亡者建立的继承国，或前往“与我们共享信仰的蛮族之地”，如保加尔人或罗斯人之地。
十五世纪约安尼斯·卡纳布泽斯对此解释得很清楚

en: one is not a barbarian on account of religion, but because of

language, the ordering of one’s politics, and education. For we are Christians and share the same faith and confession with many other nations, but we call them barbarians, I mean the Bulgarians, Vlachs, Albanians, Russians, and many others.
zh: 一个人不是因为宗教而成为蛮族，而是因为
（genos）、语言、政制与教育。因为我们是基督徒，与许多其他民族共享同一信仰和信条，但我们称他们为蛮族，我指保加尔人、弗拉赫人、阿尔巴尼亚人、罗斯人以及许多其他人。

en: There were always foreign Christians inside the empire to remind the Romans of the distinction. For example, in his monastic foundation Typikon (1083 ad), the Georgian general Gregorios Pakourianos boasted that he had fought against the Pechenegs, who attacked “not just Romanía but every
of the Christians.”
zh: 帝国内部始终有外族基督徒提醒罗马人这一区别。例如，在其修道院创建章程（Typikon，公元1083年）中，格鲁吉亚将军格里戈里奥斯·帕库里亚诺斯夸耀他曾与佩切涅格人作战，他们攻击的“不仅是罗曼尼亚，而是基督徒的每一个
（genos）”。

en: The distinction between Roman and Christian did not require a contrast with foreigners, as it could be made on grounds that were purely internal to Byzantine culture. For example,
emperors were sometimes praised as good rulers when it came to “the affairs of the Romans” while being condemned for oppressing Christians through their bad religious policies.

In condemning the rebel general Leon Sgouros, the historian Niketas Choniates puts into the mouth of his brother Michael a speech that distinguishes between the man’s Christian and Roman identities: “It was not fitting for one who was called a Christian and who was reckoned among the Romans to wage war against the Romans, unless he were paying mere lip service to Christ’s name and was, in his heart, far removed from those who are named after Him, while, as for being Roman, he was like them only with respect to his dress and speech.”

A true Roman would not only wear Roman dress and speak the Roman language (Greek), he would also be loyal and patriotic toward his fellow Romans. As a Christian, on the other side of the equation, he would exhibit appropriate moral qualities. In the early fifteenth century, the emperor Manuel II Palaiologos likewise noted that “we are Romans and Christians by
and baptism”—that is, respectively.
zh: 罗马与基督徒之间的区别不需要与外族人对照，因为它可以基于纯粹内在于拜占庭文化的理由作出。例如，
皇帝有时在涉及“罗马人的事务”时被赞为好统治者，却因其恶劣宗教政策压迫基督徒而受谴责。
在谴责叛将利奥·斯古罗斯时，历史学家尼基塔斯·霍尼亚特斯借他兄弟米海尔之口发表一番议论，把此人的基督徒身份和罗马人身份分别开来：“一个被称为基督徒、并被算在罗马人之中的人，不该对罗马人开战，除非他只是口头上尊崇基督之名，内心却远离那些以祂命名的人；而就做罗马人而言，他只在服饰与言语上与他们相似。”
一个真正的罗马人不仅会穿罗马服饰、讲罗马语言（希腊语），还要忠于罗马同胞、热爱罗马国家。基督徒身份所要求的，则是相应的道德品质。十五世纪初，皇帝曼努埃尔二世·巴列奥略同样指出“由于
（genos）和洗礼，我们是罗马人和基督徒”，两者分别对应。

en: There is, therefore, no reason to postulate an either / or between Roman and Christian or a false equivalence of the two. For the Byzantines, it was instead a both / and situation. For example, it was sometimes underscored that Byzantine civil wars were fought between people who were “
of the same race
the same faith.”
Leon VI advised his generals not to break agreements with the enemy because it would be a shameful thing for Romans to do when “the other
” are upholding their end of the bargain—“for Romans, moreover, who are also Christians.”
zh: 因此，没有理由认定罗马人和基督徒两种身份只能取其一，也没有理由把二者等同起来。拜占庭人完全可以同时拥有两种身份。例如，有时人们强调拜占庭内战是在“
同种族
同信仰”的人之间进行的。
利奥六世劝告他的将军们不要违背与敌人的协议，因为当“其他
（ethne）”都在守约时，罗马人这样做会是可耻之事——“尤其是对于既是罗马人又是基督徒的人”。

en: A monastic founder of the later eleventh century, Nikon of the Black Mountain (near Antioch), cites his Roman ethnicity as proof that he is Orthodox (i.e., Chalcedonian), in what had by then become a confusing ethnic and denominational situation in the east. He states that he himself was never curious about the fine points of doctrine but had received the faith “entire from the start and from his ancestors: these were not people who had been raised and lived in any of the places and lands where the heresies are all mixed up together, but were a Roman root (ῥίζα ‘Ρωμαίων), via the grace of Christ.”

Nikon, who was probably from Constantinople, configures his Romanness as a function of ancestry (i.e., ethnically) and uses this in turn to establish his Orthodoxy. Here we can see how ethnicity and religion, while not being the same thing, are mutually reinforcing. They are also mutually exclusive of both ethnic and doctrinal others, a dynamic that we will observe when we turn, in the second part of this book, to examine the imperial rule by Orthodox Romans over their non-Roman subjects.
zh: 十一世纪晚期一位修道院创建者、黑山（靠近安条克）的尼孔，援引自己的罗马族群性作为他是正教徒（即卡尔西顿派）的证明，当时东方已陷入一种混乱的族群与教派局面。他陈述说自己从未有意钻研教义上的细微分别，而是“从一开始并从祖先那里完整地领受了信仰：这些人不是在任何异端混杂之地成长生活的人，而是借基督之恩而成的一个罗马根脉（ῥίζα ‘Ρωμαίων）”。
尼孔大概来自君士坦丁堡，他把自己的罗马身份归于祖源，也就是从族群上理解这种身份，并据此证明自己秉持正教。这里我们可以看到族群性与宗教虽非同一事物，却相互强化。两种认同也共同把其他族群和教派排除在外。我们将在本书第二部分考察正教罗马人对非罗马臣民的帝国统治时观察到。

en: When twentieth-century historians of Byzantium played up Orthodoxy and occluded the Byzantines’ ethnic Romanness, they made it impossible to explain both foreign and domestic relations between Romans and non-Romans. Ethnic Romanness was swapped out for “universal” Christian ideals that created an alleged “ecumenical” state. These terms were never defined, but the general sense was that the “Romans” (i.e., Orthodox) could not have formed an ethnic group because they were committed to ecumenical ideals.

However, this model could not explain any of the policies of the state or the ethnic exclusivity and cultural chauvinism of its majority population. It also naively overestimated the degree to which Christianity is capable of creating universal communities of faith that transcend ethnic differences. Historically, it has tended to underwrite exclusivist national ideas and movements just as often as it has created bridges between peoples and cultures.
There is no reason to assume that it would have weakened, replaced, or subsumed Roman ethnicity. If anything, it reinforced the Romans’ sense of superiority, even toward other non-Roman Christians.
zh: 当二十世纪的拜占庭历史学家突出正教、掩盖拜占庭人的罗马族群身份，也就无从解释罗马人和非罗马人在帝国内外的关系。在这种解释里，罗马族群认同让位于“普世”的基督教理想，据说正是这种理想造就了一个“普世”国家。这些术语从未被定义，但大意是：“罗马人”（即正教徒）不可能形成一个族群，因为他们致力于普世理想。
然而这一模型无法解释国家的任何政策，也无法解释其多数人口的族群排他性与文化沙文主义。它还天真地高估了基督教创造超越族群差异的普世信仰共同体的能力。历史上，它促进各民族和文化相互沟通，也同样常常为排他的民族观念和运动提供依据。
没有理由假设它会削弱、取代或吞没罗马族群性。如果说有什么作用，它反而强化了罗马人的优越感，甚至对其他非罗马基督徒亦然。

en: There is an “ecumenical” bias in modern scholarship about Byzantium, by which I mean an assumption that Byzantine Orthodoxy was premised on those passages of the New Testament that gesture toward ethnic inclusiveness rather than the books of the Old Testament that present the Chosen People as superior to all the rest. Many studies of Byzantine identity begin with quotations from the New Testament and use the alleged “universal” or “ecumenical” spirit of the Christian message to define the realities of the Byzantine state and society. From this, the conclusion is drawn that the Byzantines did not see the world in ethnic terms and so ethnicity played no role in Byzantine social history, which flies in the face of all our evidence.

Because of these misconceptions, historians have not investigated the degree to which even Byzantine Orthodoxy complied with state projects that targeted other Christians or cultivated an ethnic Romanness that was premised on a categorical distinction between the Romans and “the nations,” especially when the latter were also Christians.

The Byzantine Church has sometimes rightly been seen as a “national Church,” as it was a pillar holding up the Roman imperial establishment, but its history and practices have not yet been studied from that standpoint.
zh: 现代拜占庭研究中存在一种“普世”偏见，我指的是这样一种假设：拜占庭正教以《新约》中那些指向族群包容的段落为前提，而非以《旧约》中那些把选民呈现为优于所有其他民族的书卷为前提。许多关于拜占庭认同的研究以《新约》引文开篇，用基督教信息据称的“普世”或“大公”精神来界定拜占庭国家与社会的现实。由此得出结论：拜占庭人不以族群方式看待世界，因此族群性在拜占庭社会史中不起任何作用——这与我们所有的证据相悖。
由于这些误解，历史学家没有考察拜占庭正教在多大程度上配合了国家针对其他基督徒的行动，或在多大程度上培育了一种把罗马人同“万民”截然分开的族群认同，尤其是当这些其他民族也信奉基督教时。
拜占庭教会有时被正确地视为一个“民族教会”，因为它是支撑罗马帝国体制的一根支柱，但其历史与实践尚未从那一立场加以研究。

en: These are big issues that will likely be explored more when scholarship opens the question, as inevitably it will, of Romanía as a national state. I here consider a few ways in which the Roman context shaped the habits, thoughts, and practices of Orthodoxy in the empire. One area that has been studied, for example, is how religion was used to boost morale in the army, fusing patriotism with religious faith even when the war was against other Christians.

It is often difficult to distinguish between “sacred war” and Roman nationalism, as the soldiers are addressed emotionally as both Romans and Christians. Moreover, the militarization of religion was not limited to army camps. Prayers on behalf of the Roman emperor, expressing the hope that he will defeat the barbarians, are expressed in many saints’ lives.

During ordinary religious services, Romans throughout the empire made similar prayers. “The church and its public worship came to provide an enduring and frequent forum in which the average Roman subject voiced his loyalty to the emperor . . . a common experience in the daily life of the provinces and capitals.”

This was certainly expected in sermons preached before the emperor or in the capital. The patriarch Photios explicitly states at the end of his Holy Friday homily that God brought forth the emperor specifically for the well-being of the
of the Romans.

The emperors asked their subjects to pray for them generally but also during specific crises. Special prayers, for example, were ordered or offered in Egypt in support of the war, probably during the Arab invasion, as we know from a papyrus fragment, and Byzantine prayer books contained specialized prayers to be recited in times of “barbarian invasion.”
Ethnic distinctions were strengthened by religion.
zh: 这些是重大的问题。等到学界开始讨论罗曼尼亚作为民族国家的问题，大概会有更多研究。那场讨论迟早会到来。这里我考虑罗马语境塑造帝国中正教的习惯、思想与实践的几种方式。例如，一个已被研究的领域是宗教如何被用来提振军队士气，把爱国主义与宗教信仰融合，即便战争是针对其他基督徒。
人们同时诉诸士兵作为罗马人和基督徒的情感，因此往往难以区分“圣战”和罗马民族主义。此外，宗教的军事化不限于军营。许多圣徒传都记载了为罗马皇帝祈祷、盼他战胜蛮族的事。
在日常宗教仪式中，帝国各地的罗马人作类似的祈祷。“教会及其公共礼拜逐渐提供了一个长期存在、人们频繁参与的场合，普通罗马臣民在其中表达对皇帝的忠诚……这是行省与都城日常生活中的一种共同经验。”
在皇帝面前或在都城布道时，人们当然也期待听到这样的话。牧首佛提乌在受难日布道的结尾明言，上帝使皇帝出世，正是为了罗马人这一
（genos）的福祉。
皇帝们要求臣民一般地为他们祈祷，也在特定危机期间祈祷。例如，据我们从一份纸草残片所知，埃及曾下令或自发献上支持战争的特别祈祷，大概是在阿拉伯入侵期间；而拜占庭祈祷书包含在“蛮族入侵”之时诵读的专门祈祷。
族群区别被宗教强化了。

en: The celebration of the liturgy throughout the empire was also framed in imperial terms. The so-called Liturgy of St. Basil, the one used primarily by the Byzantine Church between the sixth and the eleventh centuries, contains a section of prayers (the Anaphora) with the following words: “Remember, Lord, our most religious and faithful emperor . . . strengthen his arm, exalt his right hand; make his empire mighty; and subject to him all the barbarous people that delight in war. . . . Remember, Lord, all rule and authority, our brothers at court and all the army.”
A military service of the tenth century prays to the Lord: “Save your people . . . grant victories to the emperors against the barbarians, and guard your polity through the cross.”

Recited regularly by imperial subjects, such prayers bound their religious devotion to Roman projects of empire that rested on the cardinal distinction between “us” and the barbarians. This is an ethnic-imperial aspect of the “formation of the self” in Romanía that has not yet been explored.

In this respect, what took place and was intoned in churches throughout the empire was the same as what happened in the hippodrome in Constantinople, when the people came face to face with the emperors and acclaimed them in the same religio-national terms. Heralds, the representatives of the teams, and the Roman people would there engage in a long set of acclamations that called down God’s assistance for the emperors of the Romans, who are also called “the beloved of the Romans” and “the joy of the Romans.” It included the following: “We thank you, Christ our God, for breaking up the plots of the foreign
and crushing our enemies at war.”
zh: 帝国各地举行礼仪时所用的话语，也以帝国为中心。所谓的圣瓦西里礼仪，即六至十一世纪拜占庭教会主要使用的礼仪，包含一段祈祷（即“献祭祷文”Anaphora），其中有如下话语：“主啊，记念我们最虔诚、最忠信的皇帝……求你坚固他的膀臂，高举他的右手；使他的帝国强盛；使一切好战的蛮族都臣服于他……主啊，记念一切统治与权柄，我们在宫廷的弟兄以及全军。”
十世纪的一份军事礼仪向主祈祷：“拯救你的子民……赐皇帝们战胜蛮族，并借十字架护卫你的政治共同体。”
帝国臣民定期诵读这样的祈祷，他们的宗教虔诚也就同罗马帝国的事业紧密相连，而这项事业的根基在于区分“我们”和蛮族。这是罗曼尼亚中“自我之形成”的一个族群—帝国面向，尚未被探讨。
在这方面，帝国各地教堂里发生的事和吟诵的话，与君士坦丁堡赛马场上的情形相同。民众在那里当面向皇帝欢呼，用的是同样兼具宗教和民族色彩的话语。传令官、各竞技队的代表与罗马民众会在那里依次唱诵一长串欢呼词，为罗马人的皇帝祈求上帝援助，这些皇帝也被称为“罗马人所爱戴的人”与“罗马人的喜乐”。其中包括如下话语：“基督我们的上帝啊，我们感谢你，因为你瓦解了外邦
（ethne）的阴谋，在战争中粉碎了我们的敌人。”

en: Whatever “ecumenism” may have been embedded in key Christian texts was likely a dormant option for most Byzantines. Their liturgy, institutions of governance, and entertainments in the capital expressed a strong awareness of a hostile world of

“out there” from whom they, the Roman people, were protected by their emperor, army, and God. Christianity was the religion of the Romans, a component of Romanness in many contexts. “Religion is not, and cannot be, a person’s all-encompassing identity.”
zh: 无论关键基督教文本中可能嵌入了何种“普世主义”，对大多数拜占庭人而言它大概只是一种未付诸实践的可能。他们的礼仪、治理机构与都城的娱乐，都鲜明地显示出，罗马人民认为“外面”是一个充满敌意的
（ethne）的世界，他们有赖于皇帝、军队与上帝的庇护。基督教是罗马人的宗教，在许多语境中是罗马性的一个组成部分。“宗教不是、也不可能是一个人包罗万象的认同。”

en: Romanogenesis in Retrospect
zh: 回顾罗马族源生成

en: The contours of Roman ethnicity should by now be reasonably clear. We need much more research on its cultural content, “the cultural stuff” that makes up an ethnicity,
namely the institutions, social conventions, and practices that most Romans regarded as distinctive to their

at any given moment in their history. The second part of this book will turn to the non-Roman ethnic groups living in the empire and explore how some of them could become Romans by acquiring this “stuff.” This kind of assimilation implied that ethnic differences could be overcome, that non-Romans could, in time and by accepting a new cultural profile, become Roman. Before we look at how the state enabled this process and how it was viewed by the Byzantines, a reminder is in order that

the Romans of Byzantium, or their ancestors, were the products of precisely such a process. There was a time, after all, when the core regions of Romanía had no Romans. How had it come to be filled up with Romans?
zh: 罗马族群性的轮廓到现在应当相当清楚了。我们需要对其文化内容、即构成一个族群的“文化质料”
作更多研究，也就是大多数罗马人在其历史的某一具体时刻视为本
（genos）所独有的制度、社会惯例与实践。本书第二部分将转向生活在帝国中的非罗马族群，探讨其中一些如何能通过获得这种“质料”而成为罗马人。这种同化意味着族群差异可以被克服，非罗马人能够随着时间、通过接受一种新的文化面貌而成为罗马人。在考察国家如何促成这一过程、拜占庭人又如何看待它之前，不妨先想一想，拜占庭
罗马人或其祖先，都恰恰是这一过程的产物。毕竟曾有一个时期，罗曼尼亚的核心区域没有罗马人。这些地区后来怎么会遍布罗马人呢？

en: This section will eschew an objective analysis of that transformation and focus instead on what the Byzantines themselves had to say about it. Still, it is worth keeping in mind that this is a major question in ancient history that has not yet been answered satisfactorily. Plausible terms for it include
or

namely the process by which people who formerly had other ethnic, national, legal, political, and cultural identities became Roman in those categories and let their previous identifications lapse. That this did happen during the Roman empire is understood, although it has not yet been fully theorized or explored, especially for the Greek East.
Here is an example of how modern historians acknowledge this process:

或
（Romanogenesis），即先前拥有其他族群、民族、法律、政治与文化认同的人，在这些方面逐渐成为罗马人，原有的身份也随之淡去的过程。这件事在罗马帝国期间确实发生过，这一点已被理解，尽管尚未被充分理论化或探讨，尤其就讲希腊语的帝国东部而言。
以下是现代历史学家如何承认这一过程的一个例子：

en: When peoples were conquered, incorporated into provinces and, in due course of time, became part of an integrated empire, this entailed a process of ethnic disintegration or decomposition. This is the essence of “Romanization.” The Nabataeans, the Idumaeans, and the Commageneans in the east, the Allabroges in the west, all disappeared as ethnic entities.
zh: 各民族遭到征服，被并入行省，逐渐成为统一帝国的一部分，与此同时，其原有的族群也逐渐解体或瓦解。这就是“罗马化”的本质。东方的纳巴泰人、以土买人、科马吉尼人，西方的阿洛布罗基人，都作为族群实体消失了。

en: To theorize the final outcome of this Romanogenesis, historians are even beginning to experiment with the concept of “nation,” previously a dreaded word.

A separate book can (and should) be written on how the Roman nation that we call Byzantium came into being in the Greek east. Here I would like to focus on what later Byzantine sources said about it. Having access to abundant narratives from antiquity, Byzantine authors knew that Asia Minor, for example, was once not Roman, and then was full of Romans, such as themselves. How had that happened?
zh: 为了从理论上认识罗马族源生成的最终结果，历史学家甚至开始尝试使用“民族”这个概念——一个先前令人畏惧的词。
可以（而且应当）写一本专书，论述我们称为拜占庭的那个罗马民族如何在希腊东部形成。这里我想聚焦于后期拜占庭史料对此的说法。拜占庭作者能接触到丰富的古代叙事，知道小亚细亚等地原本并非罗马之地，后来却遍布罗马人，作者自己也在其列。那是如何发生的？

en: We discussed the legal aspect of this transformation in Chapter 2. But beyond acquiring a Roman legal status, how had the subjects of the empire acquired a Roman ethnicity too? Sources available to the Byzantines touched on aspects of this process. In his commentary on the book of Daniel, for example, Hippolytos (third century) tried to explain why the prophet did not offer a species-image for the nation, the Romans, that would terminate the sequence of world empires. The Babylonians, he explains, were a single nation
and so were the Persians, which is why the prophet figured them as individual animals. “But the beast that rules now is not a single
rather, it is drawn from all tongues and from every
of people, all of whom are called Romans.” Therefore, the prophet offered a composite image of them.
In this text, written probably soon after the
the Romans are understood as a single entity consisting of many ethnic groups; they are a plural
But this later shifted toward greater ethnic unity.
zh: 我们在第2章讨论了这一转化的法律方面。但除了取得罗马法律身份之外，帝国的臣民如何也取得了罗马族群性？拜占庭人可用的史料触及了这一过程的各个方面。例如，希波吕托斯（三世纪）在其《但以理书》注释中试图解释，为何先知没有用单独一种兽来描绘世界诸帝国序列中的最后一个民族，即罗马人。他解释说，巴比伦人是一个单一民族（
），波斯人也是，这就是先知把他们描绘为单个动物的原因。“但如今统治的兽不是单一的
（ethnos）；毋宁说，它由操各种语言的人和各个
（genos）组成，他们全都称为罗马人。”因此先知为他们提供了一个复合形象。
在这部大概写于《安东尼努斯敕令》之后不久的文本中，罗马人被理解为一个由许多族群构成的单一实体；他们是一个由多族组成的
（ethnos）。不过，他们后来在族群上更加趋于统一。

en: In time, the mere name “Roman” was accompanied by a more “thorough” Roman profile, as the fourth-century philosopher and court orator Themistios put it. He astutely outlined this transformation in a speech arguing that the Goths who were then being settled in the empire, admittedly not under the best circumstances, could, in time, become regular Romans, just as had happened to the Galatians of Asia Minor. The Galatians had once been ferocious Gallic barbarians, but were now ordinary Romans, no different from any others. Here is how he put it:
zh: 随着时间推移，仅有罗马名号的人逐渐有了更“彻底”的罗马特征，正如四世纪哲学家兼宫廷演说家塞米斯提乌斯所言。他在一篇演说中敏锐地勾勒出这一转化，论证当时正被安置在帝国中的哥特人——诚然不是在最好的境况下——随着时间能够成为寻常的罗马人，正如小亚细亚的加拉太人所经历的那样。加拉太人曾是凶猛的高卢蛮族，如今却是普通的罗马人，与任何其他人无异。以下是他的说法：

en: Look at these Galatians, the ones in the Pontos. These men crossed over into Asia under the law of war and, having depopulated the entire region on this side of the Halys, settled in this territory which they now inhabit. And neither Pompey nor Lucullus destroyed them, although this was perfectly possible, nor Augustus nor the emperors after him; rather, they remitted their sins and assimilated them into the empire. And now no one would ever refer to the Galatians as barbarian but as thoroughly Roman. For while their ancestral name has endured, their way of life is now akin to our own. They pay the same taxes as we do, they enlist in the same ranks as we do, they accept governors on the same terms as the rest, and abide by the same laws.
zh: 看看本都的这些加拉太人。他们凭借战争的权利渡海进入亚细亚，使哈吕斯河这边整片地区的人口绝迹，后来定居在如今所住的这片土地。庞培和卢库鲁斯本有能力灭掉他们，却没有这样做，奥古斯都和后继的诸帝也没有这样做。他们赦免了加拉太人，将其纳入帝国。如今谁也不会称加拉太人为蛮族，他们已是彻底的罗马人。尽管他们的祖传名称依然留存，生活方式却已同我们相近。他们和我们缴纳同样的税，编入同样的军伍，和其他人一样接受总督管辖，遵守同样的法律。

en: Let us focus on the factors highlighted here as facilitating Romanization. First, the Roman leadership did not try to destroy the Galatians but sought to integrate them into the Roman order (ἐν μέρει τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐποιήσαντο). Second, their way of life had adjusted to a Roman norm. Third, they lived under the same laws, taxes, and administrative arrangements as other Romans, and as a result the Galatians were eventually regarded as fellow Romans and no longer as barbarians. In sum, becoming Romans was a process of integration by which one acquired the name, customs (including language), laws, and political order as other Romans, all of which went far beyond mere citizenship. By the end of the process, the only thing that differentiated the Galatians from other provincial Romans was their “ancestral name,” which was normalized within the Roman order as the name of a province. They were just Romans from the province of Galatia. This is what an early Byzantine model of ancient Romanization might look like.
zh: 让我们聚焦于这里强调的促进罗马化的因素。第一，罗马领导层没有试图消灭加拉太人，而是设法把他们整合进罗马秩序（ἐν μέρει τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐποιήσαντο）。第二，他们的生活方式已经符合罗马人的准则。第三，他们与其他罗马人生活在同样的法律、税收与行政安排之下，结果加拉太人最终被视为同胞罗马人，不再是蛮族。总之，成为罗马人是一个整合过程，在此过程中，人们获得与其他罗马人相同的名称，采用同样的习俗（包括语言），也纳入同一法律和政治秩序，所有这些都远超单纯的公民权。到过程结束时，唯一使加拉太人区别于其他行省罗马人的是他们的“祖传名称”，这一名称在罗马秩序中已经成为一个行省的通用名称。他们只是来自加拉太行省的罗马人。这就是一个早期拜占庭式的古罗马化模型可能的样子。

en: By the early fifth century, if not before, this had resulted in the extinction of many local ethnicities and their replacement with a Roman one. Discussing the issue of ethnic diversity in his own time, Augustine (d. 430) asked rhetorically in a homily: “Who now knows which nations in the Roman empire were which, when all have become Romans and all are called Romans?”
Unlike Hippolytos, there was no longer any reason to insist on the composite nature of the beast. Provincials were not only
Romans, they

Romans. To be sure, Augustine was not an author who was available to later Byzantines, and he was saying this to highlight the relatively greater importance of the difference between Christian and non-Christian.

But it is nevertheless fascinating that he could say this. It matches what we find in eastern sources, for example the historian Agathias’ explanation of how the inhabitants of the city of Tralleis should now be regarded as mainstream ethnic Romans, regardless of who their ancestors were.
zh: 到五世纪初（如果不是更早），这已导致许多地方族群认同的消失，取而代之的是罗马族群认同。奥古斯丁（卒于430年）在讨论他那个时代的族群多样性问题时，在一篇布道中反问：“如今人人都成了罗马人，也都被称为罗马人，谁还知道罗马帝国各族原本是什么人呢？”
与希波吕托斯的时代不同，人们已经没有理由再强调那头兽由多种成分构成。行省之人不仅
罗马人，他们
罗马人。诚然，奥古斯丁不是后期拜占庭人能接触到的作者，而且他说这话是为了强调相比之下，基督徒和非基督徒的区别更为要紧。
但他能这样说仍然令人着迷。这与我们在东部史料中所见相符，例如历史学家阿加提阿斯解释特拉勒斯城的居民如今为何应被视为罗马族群中普通的一员，无论他们的祖先是谁。

en: Before looking at later Byzantine views of this process, it is, as always, worth considering Arabic perceptions, in this case that of Mas’udi (d. 956), which is substantially correct. He is talking about the Greeks:
zh: 在考察后期拜占庭人对此有何看法之前，照例也值得看看阿拉伯人的看法。这里举的是马苏迪（卒于956年）大致正确的说法，他谈的是希腊人。

en: [We rehearsed] how they [the Greeks] were defeated by the Romans
and were absorbed into their society
such that [the Greeks’] name vanished and there ceased all mention of them, and all of them were renamed Romans
after their defeat by the emperor Augustus.
zh: ［我们已经叙述过］他们［希腊人］如何败于罗马人（
），融入罗马人的社会（
）。［希腊人的］名号就此消失，也再无人提起他们。他们败于奥古斯都皇帝之后，就一概改称罗马人（

en: The Greeks were absorbed by the Romans in antiquity, just as we will see in Chapter 4 that other ethnic groups were absorbed by the Byzantine Romans.
zh: 希腊人在古代被罗马人吸纳，正如我们将在第4章看到其他族群被拜占庭罗马人吸纳。

en: Turning now to later Roman views, in his treatise

the emperor Konstantinos VII provided an antiquarian gazetteer of the empire’s provinces, drawing on classical texts and ancient ethnography and mixing with them a few recent developments. The first theme he discusses is the Anatolikon, which encompassed most of north-central Asia Minor. It is inhabited, he says, by five nations

the Phrygians, Lykaonians, Isaurians, Pamphylians, and Pisidians. Of course, these were not true ethnic groups in middle Byzantium, only the antiquarian names of Roman provinces. But Konstantinos makes an important qualification: “When the Roman yoke fell upon them, they were all subjugated and became compact [or mixed together: συμμιγεῖς] under one authority,” namely the Roman one.

The many had been mixed together into one. Konstantinos does not specify whether the five prior nations had ceased to exist and had become some other new thing, or whether the result was simply a composite of the five. It is, nevertheless, fascinating to see him take note of this issue, even if only in a passing remark.
zh: 现在转向后期罗马人的看法。皇帝君士坦丁七世在其论著《论军区》中以古典文本和古代民族志为据写了一部追溯古代沿革的帝国行省地志，也兼及少数近事。他讨论的第一个军区是安纳托利孔军区，涵盖小亚细亚中北部的大部分地区。他说，那里居住着五个民族（
）：弗里吉亚人、吕卡奥尼亚人、伊苏里亚人、潘菲利亚人与皮西迪亚人。当然，这些在拜占庭中期并非真正的族群，这些旧称所指的只是罗马行省。但君士坦丁作了一个重要限定：“当他们戴上罗马的轭，全都臣服于同一政权，结合成一个整体［或混合在一起：συμμιγεῖς］”，即罗马的统治。
多族就此合而为一。君士坦丁没有说明那五个先前的民族是否已不复存在、融成了新的民族，还是结果只是五者的复合。尽管如此，看到他注意到这一问题——即便只是一句随口的评论——仍然令人着迷。

en: The most interesting account of ancient Romanization is contained in a set of letters by the patriarch Photios (ninth century). In two letters (nos. 246–247), Photios explained to his correspondent Euschemon, the bishop of Kaisareia, how St. Paul could have been a Roman, which Euschemon was inclined to doubt on the grounds that Paul was a Jew from Tarsos in Cilicia. He later wrote a longer and more elaborate version of the argument (

103), which is addressed more generally: “To anyone who asks how is it that we can’t convict the divine Apostle of falsehood when he says that he is both a Jew and Roman, having Tarsos as his native country at one point but being born at Rome in another.”
It is in fact quite possible to doubt the claim of Acts—not made in the epistles, not even in Romans—that Paul was a Roman citizen.
But Photios maintains that Paul did not lie when he called himself either a Jew or a Roman. Let us look at his argument.
zh: 关于古罗马化最有趣的叙述，包含在牧首佛提乌（九世纪）的一组书信中。在两封信（第246–247号）中，佛提乌向通信对象凯撒利亚主教欧斯赫蒙解释，圣保罗为何可以是罗马人。欧斯赫蒙对此颇有疑问，理由是保罗是来自基利家塔尔索的犹太人。他后来写了一个更长、更详尽的论证版本（《书信》103），对象更普遍：“答一切有此疑问的人：神圣的使徒自称既是犹太人又是罗马人，有时说故乡是塔尔索，又说自己生在罗马，为什么我们不能就此认定他说了假话？”
事实上，完全可以怀疑《使徒行传》的说法——书信中并未作出，甚至《罗马书》中也没有——即保罗是罗马公民。
但佛提乌坚持保罗无论自称犹太人还是罗马人都没有撒谎。让我们看看他的论证。

en: Photios begins

103 with arguments from plausibility that we can pass by (namely that Paul would not have risked lying about this because he was being attacked by the Jews as a liar, and also that the Jews did not deny that he was a Roman citizen, thereby tacitly conceding his claim: ll. 5–40). The main question is conceptual rather than factual: How could Paul simultaneously be a Jew, a citizen of Tarsos, and a Roman? (ll. 41–44). Photios maintains that there is no problem here. Paul was a Jew by
(family or race) and by being raised in the Mosaic Law; his fatherland

was Tarsos, because he was born there; and, finally, he both was and was called a Roman because his father had obtained citizenship formally either through a Roman grant or by paying money (ll. 45–49). Thus Paul was not born “at” Rome but was born into the Roman name (i.e., citizenship) and the Roman polity (ll. 51–54).

Photios is explicit that “in those days, the dignity [of Roman citizenship] was enjoyed not only by those who were born at Rome but also by those to whom its name was formally granted by law or payment” (ll. 60–62). Moreover, it was not only individual men but entire cities and even cities of a foreign

that could acquire the Roman name. Photios cites the example of the city of Philippi, whose citizens called themselves Romans (ll. 63–75). Although he does not say so, we know that the city was made a Roman colony in the aftermath of the famous battle there in 42 bc. Photios does, however, make excellent use of the narrative in Acts 16:16–24 in order to show the adoption by the Philippians of a Roman identity. Paul had driven a spirit out from a local slave girl, which had enabled her to predict the future. Her owners took him to court, accusing him, a Jew, of trying to spread practices that were unlawful for “us Romans.” The text clearly shows that the locals had embraced a kind of Romanness, expressing it in the first person.
zh: 佛提乌以一些我们可以略过的或然性论证开始《书信》103（即保罗不会冒险在这件事上撒谎，因为他正被犹太人攻击为撒谎者；而且犹太人并未否认他是罗马公民，从而默认了他的主张：第5–40行）。主要问题是概念性的而非事实性的：保罗如何能同时是犹太人、塔尔索公民与罗马人？（第41–44行）佛提乌坚持这里没有问题。就
（genos，家族或种族）而言，保罗是犹太人，从小也依照摩西律法受教。他生在塔尔索，那里便是他的祖国（
）。他既是罗马人，也被称为罗马人，因为他的父亲或得罗马正式授予公民权，或花钱正式取得了公民权（第45–49行）。因此保罗不是生“在”罗马，而是生来就有罗马人的名号（即公民权），属于罗马政治共同体（第51–54行）。
佛提乌明确说“当时，生在罗马的人享有［罗马公民权的］尊荣，依法或付钱取得罗马名号的人也享有同样的尊荣”（第60–62行）。此外，不仅个人，而且整座城市、甚至外

（allogeneis）的城市都能取得罗马之名。佛提乌举腓立比城为例，其公民自称罗马人（第63–75行）。虽然他没有说，但我们知道该城在公元前42年那里著名的战役之后被设为罗马殖民地。然而佛提乌确实极好地利用了《使徒行传》16:16–24的叙事，以表明腓立比人对罗马认同的采纳。保罗曾从一个当地女奴身上赶出一个灵，那灵使她能预测未来。她的主人们把他告上法庭，指控他这个犹太人试图传播“我们罗马人”依法不可遵行的习俗。文本清楚表明当地人已经具备某种罗马身份，并以第一人称表明自己的身份。

en: After more arguments from narrative plausibility (ll. 76–111), Photios asks a side question: “Was he not then a Christian too? But of course he was.” This, however, was a name that he bore on behalf of his religion

a different kind of identity (ll. 112–117). So Paul’s profile is, in Photios’ account, shaping up to be compound: a Jew by race or ancestry, a Tarsian by place of birth, a Roman by citizenship, and a Christian by religion. This is interesting because it resonates with the multiple identities born by many Romans in Photios’ own time. Some Romans, for example, had a foreign ethnic ancestry (e.g., Armenian or Slavic), were Christian Orthodox in their religion, Hellenic by language (especially if they were educated), and their national, political, and legal identity was Roman.
zh: 进一步论证这些叙述何以可信之后（第76–111行），佛提乌问了一个附带问题：“那他不也是基督徒吗？但他当然是。”然而这个名称来自他的宗教（
），属于另一类身份（第112–117行）。因此在佛提乌的叙述中，保罗的面貌逐渐呈现为复合的：按种族或血统是犹太人，按出生地是塔尔索人，按公民权是罗马人，按宗教是基督徒。这很有趣，因为它呼应了佛提乌所处时代许多罗马人身兼多重身份的情况。例如，一些罗马人有外族血统（如亚美尼亚或斯拉夫），在宗教上是基督教正教徒，在语言上是希腊的（尤其如果受过教育），而其民族、政治与法律认同是罗马的。

en: Photios concludes the letter by trying to make Paul an ethnic Roman too, though he does this in a half-hearted way. He offers a tale according to which Paul’s Hebrew tribe of Benjamin had sent colonists to Italy in prehistoric times, including one Ros, the ancestor of the Romans (ll. 118–134).

Photios himself is skeptical of this tale, but it is interesting that he, an ethnic Roman, imagined that Paul’s legal Romanness needed an ethnic aspect. His letter is also interesting in that it lays out a conceptual foundation for having two, three, or more
or fatherlands, albeit configured along different existential aspects (ancestry, place of birth, religion, civic-ethnic). It is unlikely that Photios knew Cicero’s theory of the two
or two fatherlands, of each Roman, namely his place of origin and the Roman
as a whole.

Photios’ analysis replicates that distinction, which is due to the fact that both authors were thinking within the common paradigm provided by the Roman polity to which they belonged. That paradigm tended to produce similar effects, even if separated by a millennium. Both Cicero and Photios lay down a path by which both individuals and whole cities could become Roman.
zh: 佛提乌在信的结尾也试图说保罗在族群上是罗马人，不过口气并不坚决。他提供一个故事，说保罗所属的希伯来便雅悯支派曾在史前时代派殖民者到意大利，其中包括一个罗斯（Ros），罗马人的祖先（第118–134行）。
佛提乌自己对这个故事持怀疑态度，但有趣的是，他作为一个族群罗马人，认为保罗在法律上既是罗马人，也应该有某种族群上的依据。这封信还有趣的是，它为拥有两个、三个或更多
（patridai）奠定了概念基础，不过它们各有不同的依据（血统、出生地、宗教、公民—族群）。佛提乌不大可能知道西塞罗关于每个罗马人有两个
（patriae）的理论，即他的出身之地与作为整体的罗马
（res publica）。
佛提乌的分析作出了相同的区分，这是由于两位作者都在他们所属罗马政治共同体提供的共同范式内思考。那一范式往往产生相似的效果，即便相隔一千年。西塞罗与佛提乌都阐明了一条途径，使个人与整座城市都能成为罗马人。

en: The letters to Euschemon provide more historical and conceptual support for this mode of analysis. In the brief

246, Photios distinguishes among the Apostle’s various fatherlands. First, he was a citizen of heavenly Jerusalem through his love of Christ. Second, his distant ancestors were from the Judaean village of Gischala, which made this his
through the link provided by birth. Third, Tarsos was also his
as he was born there. Finally, the Romans were so magnanimous that they bestowed their name and citizenship even on people who were not of the same
or race, as themselves. In this way, Paul’s parents acquired Rome as their
and polity through “human laws,” as opposed to the bonds of ethnicity. This is what Paul meant when he told the centurion that he was “born a Roman.” Thus, Paul had not only two
but three (or four, if we add heavenly Jerusalem).
zh: 致欧斯赫蒙的书信为这种分析模式提供了更多历史与概念支持。在简短的《书信》246中，佛提乌区分了使徒的各个祖国。第一，他因对基督的爱而是天上耶路撒冷的公民。第二，他的远祖来自犹太地的吉斯卡拉村，出身使那里也成为他的
（patris）。第三，塔尔索也是他的
，因为他生在那里。最后，罗马人如此宽宏大量，甚至把他们的名称与公民权授予那些与他们不同
（phylon，即种族）的人。以这种方式，保罗的父母通过“人的法律”、而非族群纽带，得以把罗马视为自己的
，并成为罗马政治共同体的成员。这就是保罗告诉百夫长他“生为罗马人”时的意思。因此保罗不仅有两个
（patridai），而是三个（如果加上天上耶路撒冷则是四个）。

en: In

247, Photios mentions the Apostles Barnabas and Apollos in order to draw a distinction among the affiliations that one has by ancestry (e.g., a Jew), by place of birth (e.g., a Cypriot), and through residence in a city (e.g., an Alexandrian). After applying this distinction to Paul, he makes the point about the city of Philippi: it managed to glorify itself with the name of Rome even though, as a Macedonian city, it had no kinship relation with Rome. In this letter, Photios also raises the example of the historian Josephos. He too was a Jew whose

was Jerusalem, but he acquired Roman citizenship, which he signaled through the name Flavius (after Vespasian, his patron). In fact, when Jerusalem itself was renamed Aelia Capitolina by Hadrian and made a part of the Roman polity, it too “put on a Roman
so that all of them, even though their
and their
were of a different race, were registered in the Roman polity.”

Jerusalem had thereby acquired a Roman identity. We can detect in Photios’ language his pride in being a Roman in the same tradition, as he claims that all these people and places were “honored and dignified” at receiving the Roman name (ἐπισεμνύνουσι).
zh: 在《书信》247中，佛提乌提到使徒巴拿巴与亚波罗，以区分一个人按血统（如犹太人）、按出生地（如塞浦路斯人）、以及通过居住在一座城市（如亚历山大里亚人）所拥有的归属。把这一区别应用于保罗之后，他就腓立比城提出一点：它以获得罗马之名为荣，尽管作为一座马其顿城市，它与罗马没有亲缘关系。在这封信中，佛提乌还举了历史学家约瑟夫斯的例子。他也是犹太人，其
（patris）是耶路撒冷，但他取得了罗马公民权，并通过弗拉维乌斯这个名字标示出来（取自他的庇护者韦斯巴芗）。事实上，当耶路撒冷本身被哈德良改名为埃利亚·卡皮托利纳、并被纳入罗马政治共同体时，它也“跻身罗马人的
（genos）。这些人虽出自别的
（ethnos），来自别的
（patris），也都登记入籍，成为罗马公民”。
耶路撒冷由此取得了一种罗马认同。我们能在佛提乌的语言中察觉他作为同一传统中罗马人的自豪，因为他声称所有这些人与地方在获得罗马之名时都“受尊荣、得尊贵”（ἐπισεμνύνουσι）。

en: Among all Romans, Photios thought the hardest about the conceptual issues posed by Romanization in antiquity. He did so because he had to defend the Apostle against the accusation of lying about being Roman. In order to do so he had to draw analytical distinctions among different types of affiliation (such as ancestry, city of origin, religion, and citizenship) that ancient and medieval thought tended, by default, to lump together under the rubric of a single unified identity. In the process, Photios also provides a flexible analytical framework by which we can understand the articulated complexity of Romanía itself, which was absolutely a Roman civilization, albeit one that was not located physically in Italy, did not speak Latin, nor practiced ancient Roman religion. Photios tried to understand how one could acquire a Roman
and
even if one’s

was originally foreign. He correctly distinguishes between being Roman and being Christian, and provides a model by which one can acquire Roman ethnicity without a Roman ancestry. If ancestry was necessary, it could always be invented. Jews had, after all, colonized ancient Italy.
zh: 在所有罗马人中，佛提乌对古罗马化提出的概念问题思考得最深入。他这样做是因为他必须为使徒辩护，反驳说他谎称自己是罗马人的指控。为了做到这一点，他必须在不同类型的归属（如血统、出身城市、宗教与公民权）之间作出分析性区分，而古代和中世纪的人往往不加区分，把它们都算作同一种身份。在这一过程中，佛提乌还提供了一个灵活的分析框架，有助于理解罗曼尼亚各种身份交织的复杂情况。罗曼尼亚无疑是罗马文明，尽管它地处意大利之外，说的不是拉丁语，奉行的也不是古罗马宗教。佛提乌试图理解一个人如何能加入罗马
（genos），取得罗马
（politeia），即便此人原本属于外族（
）。他正确地区分了做罗马人与做基督徒，并提供了一个模型，使人能在没有罗马血统的情况下成为罗马族群的一员。真要讲究血统，总可以编造一套谱系。毕竟，犹太人曾殖民古代意大利。
